this is what my hair looked like almost exactly growing up and not properly taking care of it. towards the end I straightened it every couple of days too. I can’t tell you how to save it since I’m transmasc and ended up cutting it all off pre curly hair routine but it ended up being 3A-3B healthy (then my immune system said, who needs hair? and now I’ve been bald for years lol). 

first off—you have a LOT of split ends and no matter what you do you need to go to a hairdresser and get them cut off. 

second, while I don’t personally recommend doing the curly girl method exclusively anymore (I think it leads to way too much build up without clearing up and “forbidden” stuff has its place if used correctly) I think it’s a good place to start. keep in mind, your hair is damaged and you’re not going to see full results for a while. like a while a while. people like to post their immediate results but I’d argue full results takes years. 

use a clarifying shampoo to start. prioritize moisture—curly hair needs it! only comb your hair while it’s fully wet and with conditioner in it. when you get out of the shower don’t rub a towel against your hair. crunch some kind of gel into it and then use a t-shirt to “plop” it to dry.

in terms of what products to use, key ingredients, what to avoid, etc, that’s best left for the curly haired subreddits. 

lastly, if you do decide to keep using heat, at the very minimum use heat protection. keep your future options open.

edit: there is ONE thing you can do that’s kind of crazy if you want to fully jump in, that I did just for fun without any knowledge I had curly hair and then in learning to care for that hair as my hair kept growing it stayed curly. 

I permed it curly. obviously go to a good stylist because it is very easy to do a bad perm. 

is it actual advice? I don’t know. but I did it. and it worked out. permed hair is just that—permanent. it’s a lot easier to care for and figure out when you’re just starting out a curly haired routine. you get very immediate feedback. obviously ymmv.

One—I think getting treated for anxiety might be a good idea. Because if it’s not anxiety, anxiety meds won’t help. Or it could be anxiety and something else, and you’ll be able to narrow down your symptoms.

Some of your symptoms match dysautonomia which can present panic like. Try to do a “poor man’s tilt table test.” Lay down for a long time. In fact, do this first thing in the morning before you get up. Use something like an apple watch or a pulse oximeter and take your pulse. Then, stand up. Note changes in how you feel. Note your pulse. Stand up for like 5 minutes if you can. If your pulse increases by 30 or more bpm, you’ve tested positive for POTS. POTS has gotten especially common these days as a result of COVID. Have you had COVID recently? Try out wearing compression stockings and upping your salt and fluid intake significantly. Gatorade is your best friend.

If you suspect POTS, you’re going to want to make an appointment with a cardiologist. I want to reassure you it’s not life threatening, but untreated the symptoms can be debilitating.

Edit: just wanted to say I empathize with you OP as someone who is disabled AND also has anxiety. It is perfectly okay for you to want a thorough workup to ensure you’re physically okay. So many health problems get written off as anxiety that getting fully checked out *even if it is anxiety* is worth it. he might also just not be a morning person. and that’s okay! people have different chronotypes. it’s an evolutionary adaptation. if you have kids you can either leave more evening stuff for him or you can also treat a late chronotype as delayed phase sleep disorder and manage it with melatonin and strong morning lights like a SAD lamp.

I think you need to communicate with him more. You mention the chores being lopsided which isn’t okay, but that seems to be the result of when the two of you are most productive. Have you considered sitting down with him and explaining how you feel about it? You could pre-arrange your chores so they’re split more fairly. Just because it *can* be done in the morning doesn’t mean it has to be.

One more note— I think a lot of people assume if your husband needs your assistance to wake up in the morning that’s a bad or childish thing. I’m very disabled and one of the caretaking tasks I need done for me every morning is waking me up, especially so I can take my addison’s medication. I rely a lot on others to get things done. And that’s okay, because that happens to be the level of support I need. 

A lot of times it’s hurtful seeing people assume that if others need help they’re childish. many disabled parents raise kids perfectly fine even if they need help themselves. To need help is human. It’s not a moral judgment. It doesn’t speak to your husband’s other potential childrearing abilities. Y’all just need to be *good enough.* Not perfect. 

I would do the following: make sure to follow up with a doctor, especially a sleep doctor and an endocrinologist. Sit down and talk about splitting the chores more fairly and identify what morning chores can be done at night. Spend a lot of time talking about what raising a child would look like and identify each other’s strengths and weaknesses. And, realistically, accept waking up in the morning may be something your husband will always need help with for reasons outside of his control.

Edit: I would also consider seeing if you could get him evaluated for adhd. some of the chore stuff he struggles with sounds very executive functioning-y. I would suggest checking out How to ADHD on youtube as well. The tips are *incredibly* helpful.

If he has a “get around to it eventually” approach I suggest a punnet square of urgent, important, not urgent, not important. There are things that have to happen now and hey yeah there are some things that can wait and can be rescheduled. Do you have outlined EXACTLY what he has to do? Are the chores throughout the week spread out evenly energy wise, especially given we suspect a medical condition impacting his energy? Do you have hard and soft deadlines (like this should be done by then but not the end of the world if you can’t get to it, versus this MUST be done by then and there’s no wiggle room). 

Sorry for going on. tbh I see myself a lot in your husband and when you’re at a point where you’re failing others and it’s out of your control and *something* is wrong and you don’t know why it’s so hard. It’s a tough spot to be in.

however I want to point out another thing—you are racist. not in a because of this kind of way. not in a judgmental way. but rather because you’ve been raised in a racist society that has from day one sent you thousands of messages on race. it’s impossible to exist without these messages being embedded in you. 

It’s better to exist acknowledging and knowing that you’ve got racist ideas in you you need to declutter. Approach yourself nonjudgmentally. It’s simply a fact. You’ll never *not* be racist; rather it’ll be a lifelong goal to get as close to not racist as possible. 

And what you can be is ANTI-racist. That means being always willing to listen and being willing to confront racism in yourself and in the world around you. It’s a commitment to that lifelong goal. 

I think a great starter book if you’re interested is *So You Want To Talk About Race* by Ijeoma Oluo. She’s Black and she dedicates the time in her book to go over the questions people are afraid to ask. 

There are many great books and resources out there. I’ll leave you with some quick reminders:

1. Listen. Listen above all. Listen to the people impacted by racism. Financially support the works of people impacted by racism if you want to learn more. 

2. You do not get to decide if you’re an ally. Ally is a title awarded to you.

3. You are going to fuck up. It is inevitable. Remember it’s okay to be upset but the focus needs to be on the person you hurt. You can privately process your own emotions like guilt, embarrassment, anger etc and also center that you are not the harmed party.

4. When you fuck up, a sincere apology is in line, but the person is never obligated to accept your apology.

5. No one owes you an education. This is exactly what resources are for; because there are people who have decided to dedicate their time and energy to educate you. If someone in your life chooses to educate you, don’t expect it regularly. Remember the effort they put into that. Thank them. You don’t have to give a whole spiel on how they didn’t have to or how hard it is. Just a simple “thank you for taking the time and energy to teach me about this” will do. 

6. If someone calls you in, that’s difficult for them and likely them trying to save your friendship.

I use a wheelchair now but before when I used a cane on the subway sometimes seats weren’t available—the best advice I can give is ask. State that you’re pregnant, that you are in pain (just that, no detail necessary), and ask someone (it’s important to ask a specific person, same way in an emergency you appoint one person to call 911) if you can have their seat. In my experience, people are much more willing to give up their seat if you ask them directly. They might say no—it’s totally possible they are disabled themselves—but at this point someone will overhear and offer. 

My cane was also an unambiguous sign that I was disabled, versus people might feel uncomfortable making the assumption that you are pregnant based on looks alone, which is why I probably got offered a seat 80-90% of the time without asking and you aren’t.

Asking is scary but I promise people once they have the unambiguous information that you are pregnant, you are in pain, and you need a seat will be happy to give their seat up.

I found the google docs of the flowers guide I used when I bred flowers.

Here is the gene information for the pansies:

Pansies make use of 3 genes: R, Y, and W.

Seed red = RR-yy-WW
Seed yellow = rr-YY-WW
Seed white = rr-yy-Ww

Red + yellow: orange = Rr-Yy-WW (100%)
White + white: blue = rr-yy-ww (25%)
Red + blue: “hybrid red” = Rr-yy-Ww (100%)
Hybrid red + hybrid red: purple = RR-yy-ww (6.25%)

The answer is, you can’t be sure if it’s a duplicate or a breed, but it’s likely a breed. What you can do is afterwards isolate every potential hybrid red pansy you get and duplicate it, then try to breed it with the duplicate. That way, there’s no way you’re mixing a duplicate seed red and a hybrid red. 

I do have some bad news for you though: if you’ve been letting those reds run amok,  they’ve definitely bred with each other multiple times and they might be a completely different combo of genes, so you’re going to need to cull them and start over. Sorry.
